questions.q: Which tier of Microsoft Purview does this practice lab use?
options: You must purchase a separate license for every exercise
A tier that doesn't actually exist
The free version — it covers registration, scanning, classification, and catalog browsing
Only the most expensive enterprise tier, with no free option
questions.explain: The lab is designed to work with Purview's free version, which covers every exercise's core steps without requiring a paid subscription.

questions.q: What does this lesson explicitly warn against when choosing a data source for the lab?
options: Using Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 as a source
Pointing any exercise at real production or customer data — use sample or synthetic data only
Working through the exercises in order
Creating more than one collection
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that real production or customer data should never be used for these practice exercises — a throwaway sample or synthetic source is required instead.

questions.q: In Exercise 4, what makes a glossary term definition pass the 'four-part test' referenced in this lesson?
options: It's exactly one word long
It's written by an AI with no human review
It references a specific SQL query or column name directly
It's specific, self-contained, measurable where possible, and free of implementation detail
questions.explain: The four-part test (from earlier in the Data Governance career path) requires a definition to be specific, self-contained, measurable where possible, and free of implementation detail like a query or column name.

questions.q: What are the three self-check questions this lesson says you should be able to answer before moving on?
options: Name it, rename it, and archive it
Find it (search the catalog), trace it (explain its lineage), and defend it (justify its label and rule)
Delete it, rebuild it, and rescan it
Price it, ship it, and market it
questions.explain: The lesson's self-check is explicitly: can you find the asset in the catalog, trace its lineage out loud, and defend why its sensitivity label and data quality rule are the right choices.

questions.q: What should you do if, during the self-check, one of the three items feels shaky?
options: Assume it doesn't matter since the lab is optional
Delete your Purview account entirely
Ignore it and move straight to the next course
Go back and revisit the relevant earlier lesson, rather than pushing forward
questions.explain: The lesson frames the self-check as a tool for surfacing gaps while they're still cheap to fix — the right response to a shaky answer is to revisit the relevant lesson, not to push forward.
